controls.breaker_class: 3 same-class failures halts the wave and escalates
controls.idempotency: every converted job is a full recompute of its input partition for an explicit execution_date (P3-D08), so a second run overwrites with the same bytes. Proven by an actual rerun, never asserted
controls.namespace_isolation: a batch writes only its declared write_targets; DDL for a table belongs to exactly one unit. The five units share no output table, which is why this wave fans out at all
controls.fixture_vs_live: develop against the wave-0 fixture snapshot, then exactly one merge-evidence recon run per unit; a fixture PASS is never merge evidence
controls.fanout: five genuinely independent units, run through run_workflow at width 5. No unit reads another's output in this wave - user_activity_daily does, which is why it is wave 2 and not here
controls.schedules: no unit in this wave creates a schedule. Orchestration is wave 3, and every schedule it creates lands PAUSED

BATCH p3-w1-a - etl/scripts/analytics_daily.py (452 lines) -> Lakeflow Job +
SQL on Delta.

WHAT THIS BATCH IS
The daily product-analytics aggregate. The Python is a query written in loops;
it belongs in SQL on Delta. Use PySpark only for the genuinely row-wise part
(envelope parsing on ingest), not for the aggregation.

Traps, all of them contract:
 - SQS is destructive: receive+delete drains the queue, so a rerun of the
   legacy sees less input than the first run. P3-D01: land events durably in
   ow_tp.bronze.analytics_events_raw and recompute from there. That is what
   makes the target idempotent at all;
 - event types are matched as EXACT snake_case literals (F-0.9). A dotted
   'document.created' raises total_events and the hourly bucket and attributes
   its user, but contributes to no document or file metric. Reproduce that.
   Do NOT normalise the two vocabularies together - it changes the numbers;
 - active_users EXCLUDES the literal 'unknown'; top_users INCLUDES it and it is
   usually the largest row (C-2.7). The two disagree by design;
 - the eventType/event_type fallback is COLUMN-level, not row-level (C-2.9):
   if any row has eventType, rows missing it get NaN, not 'unknown';
 - malformed and absent timestamps both fall into hour '00' (C-2.8), and hour
   is a zero-padded string, not an int;
 - the Postgres upsert failure is SWALLOWED by the legacy (C-2.16). P3-D02:
   the target fails the task loudly instead. Approved behaviour change;
 - F-0.10: one non-numeric sizeBytes makes the legacy's pandas .sum() raise and
   the whole run exits 1 having written nothing. The estate cannot currently
   produce it (file-service types size_bytes u64), so it is a latent fault:
   state what the target does with such a record rather than inheriting it.

RECON
  python3 databricks/migration/recon/with_databricks_sql_token.py DATABRICKS_MIGRATION_SQL -- \
  python3 -m recon.cli run --unit p3-analytics-daily --family databricks \
    --mapping .migration/units/p3-analytics-daily/mapping_spec.json \
    --tolerances .migration/03_recon_tolerances.json \
    --mode live --source-dsn-secret DATABRICKS_MIGRATION_SQL \
    --target-kind databricks --target-secret DATABRICKS_MIGRATION_SQL \
    --target-catalog ow_tp --target-schema gold \
    --allowed-targets-file .migration/allowed_targets.json \
    --seed 0 --depth full --out .migration/recon/p3-analytics-daily/

BATCH p3-w1-b - etl/scripts/storage_cleanup_daily.py (217 lines) -> Lakeflow Job.
THE ONE-WAY DOOR. Read this batch's brief twice.

WHAT THIS BATCH IS
The legacy lists S3 objects under files/, scans DynamoDB for referenced
s3_keys, copies the orphans to quarantine and DELETES the originals. It has no
dry-run flag.

P3-D03, approved at STOP C, is binding:
 - the converted job COMPUTES and PERSISTS the delete set and does not delete;
 - deletion sits behind an explicit human-set enable flag, default OFF;
 - the flag is only unlocked after exact set equality against the legacy
   delete set on (key, size) - key alone would not catch a truncating copy;
 - nothing in this wave turns the flag on. Not once, not for a test.

Baseline isolation is not optional: the legacy runs against a per-run clone
bucket seeded from the immutable snapshot, the target reads the snapshot only
and writes no S3 at all. The two sides must never share mutable objects, or
the target would be reading state the legacy already deleted.

Also a STOP E fact, not something to fix: the bucket config.ini points at does
not exist in this estate, so the legacy cannot be deleting anything here.

RECON
  python3 databricks/migration/recon/with_databricks_sql_token.py DATABRICKS_MIGRATION_SQL -- \
  python3 -m recon.cli run --unit p3-storage-cleanup --family databricks \
    --mapping .migration/units/p3-storage-cleanup/mapping_spec.json \
    --tolerances .migration/03_recon_tolerances.json \
    --mode live --source-dsn-secret DATABRICKS_MIGRATION_SQL \
    --target-kind databricks --target-secret DATABRICKS_MIGRATION_SQL \
    --target-catalog ow_tp --target-schema silver \
    --allowed-targets-file .migration/allowed_targets.json \
    --seed 0 --depth full --out .migration/recon/p3-storage-cleanup/

BATCH p3-w1-c - etl/scripts/audit_archive_weekly.py (224 lines) -> Lakeflow Job.

WHAT THIS BATCH IS
Weekly archive of audit events older than 90 days. Three record shapes give
three different legacy behaviours and ALL THREE are contract (F-0.4/a/b):
 - A-estate (what audit-service actually writes: id/Id/Timestamp): the scan
   filters on lowercase 'timestamp', DynamoDB treats a missing attribute as a
   non-match, so it matches ZERO records, exits 0, and writes no archive and no
   compliance report. The target must also produce nothing. An empty target is
   the PASS here, not a gap;
 - A-tsonly (lowercase timestamp, no event_id): archive uploaded, then an
   uncaught KeyError -> exit 1. Archive-written-then-fail is a real path and a
   retry re-uploads under the same key;
 - A-full (lowercase timestamp + event_id): archive uploaded, every delete
   raises on the wrong key schema and is swallowed by `except: pass`, and the
   compliance report claims events_deleted_from_source 0.

P3-D04: the target archives and NEVER deletes from DynamoDB. Both sides report
zero source deletions; assert that agreement, do not assume it.

RECON
  python3 databricks/migration/recon/with_databricks_sql_token.py DATABRICKS_MIGRATION_SQL -- \
  python3 -m recon.cli run --unit p3-audit-archive --family databricks \
    --mapping .migration/units/p3-audit-archive/mapping_spec.json \
    --tolerances .migration/03_recon_tolerances.json \
    --mode live --source-dsn-secret DATABRICKS_MIGRATION_SQL \
    --target-kind databricks --target-secret DATABRICKS_MIGRATION_SQL \
    --target-catalog ow_tp --target-schema silver \
    --allowed-targets-file .migration/allowed_targets.json \
    --seed 0 --depth full --out .migration/recon/p3-audit-archive/

BATCH p3-w1-d - UsageRollupJob.scala + UsageRollupAggregator.scala (150 lines)
-> SQL on Delta. One unit: the aggregator is only ever called by the job.

WHAT THIS BATCH IS
P3-D06: this becomes SQL on Delta. NO spark_jar_task, NO cluster. Nothing in
the aggregation needs the JVM - it is a group-by with a signed running total.

 - the input uses the DOTTED analytics-service vocabulary ('document.created',
   'file.uploaded'), NOT the snake_case vocabulary analytics_daily consumes
   (F-0.9). Do not share an event-type mapping between the two units;
 - storage_bytes is signed: storage.allocated adds, storage.released
   subtracts, so it can legitimately go negative. Do not clamp it at zero;
 - F-0.6, a STOP E question and not yours to resolve: the estate's CronJob
   writes this rollup to an emptyDir that is destroyed on pod exit, so nothing
   in this repo consumes the output. Migrate it (P3-D07: it is cheap and the
   Delta table is durable and useful), and carry the question of whether its
   input and consumer are real into STOP E. Claim nothing about production.

RECON
  python3 databricks/migration/recon/with_databricks_sql_token.py DATABRICKS_MIGRATION_SQL -- \
  python3 -m recon.cli run --unit p3-usage-rollup --family databricks \
    --mapping .migration/units/p3-usage-rollup/mapping_spec.json \
    --tolerances .migration/03_recon_tolerances.json \
    --mode live --source-dsn-secret DATABRICKS_MIGRATION_SQL \
    --target-kind databricks --target-secret DATABRICKS_MIGRATION_SQL \
    --target-catalog ow_tp --target-schema gold \
    --allowed-targets-file .migration/allowed_targets.json \
    --seed 0 --depth full --out .migration/recon/p3-usage-rollup/

BATCH p3-w1-e - etl/scripts/search_reindex_weekly.py (319 lines)
-> NO DATABRICKS JOB. This batch writes a document, not a pipeline.

P3-D05, approved at STOP C: this unit is REMOVED from Databricks scope. It
reads two live in-cluster HTTP services (document-service, file-service) and
writes a MeiliSearch index (F-0.7). No step of it touches anything Databricks
can host, there is no target table, and there would be nothing to reconcile.

The deliverable is an honest coverage-gap record: what the job does, why it
does not belong on Databricks, what stays running service-side, and who owns
it. Do NOT create a placeholder job, a stub notebook, or a schedule to make
the pipeline look complete. A fake job that cannot be reconciled is worse than
a declared gap.

No recon is due: there is no converted unit to reconcile.

behaviour_changes.change: SQS receive+delete is destructive, so the legacy is not re-runnable. The target lands events durably in bronze and recomputes from there.
The legacy swallows a Postgres/serving-layer failure and reports success. The target fails the task loudly.
The legacy deletes from S3 unconditionally. The target computes the delete set and does not delete until a human sets an enable flag, gated on exact (key, size) set equality.
The target archives audit events but never deletes from DynamoDB. The legacy intends to delete and fails to; the target does not intend to.
search_reindex_weekly.py is removed from Databricks scope and stays service-side. Declared coverage gap, no substitute job.
behaviour_changes.why_untestable: There is no converted unit to test; the gap itself is the record.

behaviour_changes.change: The Scala rollup becomes SQL on Delta rather than a spark_jar_task.
execution_date becomes an explicit job parameter. The legacy derives it from datetime.now() at start, so it has no backfill path at all.

invariants.no_deletion: No unit in this wave deletes anything from S3 or DynamoDB, on any code path, under any flag value reachable in this wave.
invariants.secrets_by_name: No literal from etl/config.ini appears in converted code, a log, a notebook output, an artefact or a PR body.
invariants.empty_is_a_result: Where the legacy produces nothing (A-estate, empty input), the target produces nothing and the recon compares two empty sets. An empty target is never reported as a coverage gap.
invariants.on_violation: Any of the above would be a halt reported to the parent, never reconciled around.
